# Ring of Nestor

The Ring of Nestor is a gold signet ring that has become one of the most discussed artifacts of Aegean archaeology, noted for its elaborate engraved scene and its role in debates over Minoan and Mycenaean religious imagery, cultural contacts, and issues of authenticity. Originally published by Arthur Evans as part of a sepulchral treasure of gold signet rings and bead-seals from a burial at Thisbê in Boeotia, the ring has since been linked in scholarship with the wider Mycenaean world, including the region of Pylos and the Palace of Nestor. Its complex iconography, often interpreted as depicting a vision of the afterlife or a ritual scene, has made it a key reference point in discussions of Aegean religion and elite funerary symbolism. [4][16][17][18][19][1]

## Disclosed Conflicts

Public sources still contain unresolved disagreement on the following point: 关于“涅斯托尔指环”真实性的评价存在冲突：Evans 及后续部分学者（如 Vlachopoulos、iconography 论文作者）倾向认为戒指为真品或至少古代作品，与晚期爱琴宗教图像传统有联系；而《The Pseudo-Minoan Nestor Ring and Its Egyptian Iconography》作者则将戒指界定为“伪米诺斯”，强调其埃及图像来源并质疑其作为纯正米诺斯或迈锡尼原作的身份. [9][4][6][1]
